#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Append one provisioning entry to the users configuration.

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT

# shellcheck source=lib/format.sh
source "${ROOT}/lib/format.sh"

name=''
login_shell='/bin/bash'
out="${ROOT}/config/users.conf"

while (($# > 0)); do
  case "$1" in
    --name)
      name="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --shell)
      login_shell="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --out)
      out="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
      exit 64
      ;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p -- "$(dirname -- "${out}")"
format_line "${name}" "${login_shell}" >> "${out}"
printf 'wrote %s for %s\n' "${out}" "${name}"

.PHONY: test

test:
	@find . -name '*_test.sh' -print0 | xargs -0 -r -n1 bash
# Formatting helpers for the provisioning configuration.
# shellcheck shell=bash

# Formats one users.conf entry.
# Arguments: account name, login shell
# Outputs: the formatted line on stdout
format_line() {
  printf '%s:%s\n' "$1" "$2"
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Coverage for lib/format.sh.

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT

# shellcheck source=lib/format.sh
source "${ROOT}/lib/format.sh"

result="$(format_line alice /bin/bash)"
if [[ ${result} != 'alice:/bin/bash' ]]; then
  printf 'format_line returned %s\n' "${result}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

printf 'ok lib/format.sh\n'
root:/bin/bash

p='bin/mkuser-config.sh'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''mkdir -p --''','''if [[ -z ${name} ]]; then
  printf 'error: --name must not be empty\\n' >&2

fi

mkdir -p --''',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cat > bin/mkuser-config_test.sh <<'E'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Coverage for bin/mkuser-config.sh.

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
readonly ROOT
script="${ROOT}/bin/mkuser-config.sh"

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "${tmp}"' EXIT

fail() {
  printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Empty name is rejected: non-zero status, clear message, nothing written.
out="${tmp}/empty.conf"
err="$("${script}" --name '' --out "${out}" 2>&1 >/dev/null)"
status=$?
((status != 0)) || fail 'empty --name exited 0'
[[ ${err} == *'--name must not be empty'* ]] || fail "unclear message: ${err}"
[[ ! -s ${out} ]] || fail 'empty --name wrote an entry'

# Omitted name is rejected too.
"${script}" --out "${out}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail 'missing --name exited 0'
[[ ! -s ${out} ]] || fail 'missing --name wrote an entry'

# Valid name still works.
out="${tmp}/ok.conf"
"${script}" --name alice --out "${out}" >/dev/null || fail 'valid name failed'
[[ "$(cat "${out}")" == 'alice:/bin/bash' ]] || fail 'unexpected entry'

printf 'ok bin/mkuser-config.sh\n'
E
chmod +x bin/mkuser-config_test.sh; make test; git status --short

The new test, `bin/mkuser-config_test.sh`, sits next to the script and is picked up by `make test`. It checks four things:
- An empty name exits non-zero with the message and writes nothing.
- A missing `--name` is rejected and writes nothing.
- A valid name still writes `alice:/bin/bash`.
- The output file is a temp file, so `config/users.conf` is untouched.

I haven't committed anything.
